items.title: David Weinstein Interview, 1988-09-22
items.q: Sharkey called me long distance... he needed some material... I'd write a sketch and send it up to him that recorded... And these are the things he recorded.

ctx.x: been a great regret. You had something to do with the recording sessions that Sharkey did in New York

in the late 30s. Oh! Yes, I did. And Benny Pollack got this date for Sharkey, and Sharkey called me long distance, and in those days that was quite a thing when you got a long distance call, you know, that he needed some material. That he had, not a contract, but he had an agreement he'd make so many sides, I think for Decca, and he needed some tunes. And I was always pretty good at making little tunes, you know, to sound like Dixley and tunes. So I'd write a sketch and send it up to him that recorded. I'd write…
What was the name of the album? That's a good question. Obviously you didn't go out and buy many jazz records. You didn't buy your own.
